Let
\[
u=1-x.
\]
Near the only point where the Gaussian center touches the astroid, namely \((1,0)\), the domain has cross-section
\[
|y|\le g(u):=\left(1-(1-u)^{2/3}\right)^{3/2},\qquad u\ge 0.
\]
All parts of the domain with \(u\ge \delta>0\) are exponentially small, so only small \(u\) matters.

Expand
\[
1-(1-u)^{2/3}
=\frac23u+\frac19u^2+O(u^3)
=\frac23u\left(1+\frac16u+O(u^2)\right).
\]
Hence
\[
g(u)=\left(\frac23\right)^{3/2}u^{3/2}\left(1+\frac14u+O(u^2)\right).
\]
Put
\[
u=n^{-1/2}s,\qquad y=n^{-3/4}t.
\]
Then \(dx\,dy=du\,dy=n^{-5/4}ds\,dt\), and
\[
e^{-n(u^2+y^2)}
=e^{-s^2}e^{-n^{-1/2}t^2}
=e^{-s^2}\left(1-n^{-1/2}t^2+O(n^{-1})\right).
\]
Also
\[
n^{3/4}g(n^{-1/2}s)
=a s^{3/2}\left(1+\frac14n^{-1/2}s+O(n^{-1})\right),
\qquad a=\left(\frac23\right)^{3/2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
M_n=n^{-5/4}\int_0^\infty e^{-s^2}
\int_{-a s^{3/2}(1+\frac14n^{-1/2}s+O(n^{-1}))}^{a s^{3/2}(1+\frac14n^{-1/2}s+O(n^{-1}))}
\left(1-n^{-1/2}t^2+O(n^{-1})\right)\,dt\,ds.
\]
Thus
\[
M_n
=n^{-5/4}A+n^{-7/4}B+o(n^{-7/4}),
\]
where
\[
A=2a\int_0^\infty s^{3/2}e^{-s^2}\,ds
=a\Gamma(5/4)
=\frac{\sqrt6\,\Gamma(1/4)}{18},
\]
matching the subtracted term.

For the next coefficient,
\[
B=\int_0^\infty e^{-s^2}
\left(\frac a2 s^{5/2}-\frac23a^3s^{9/2}\right)\,ds.
\]
Using
\[
\int_0^\infty s^p e^{-s^2}\,ds=\frac12\Gamma\left(\frac{p+1}{2}\right),
\]
we get
\[
B=\frac a4\Gamma(7/4)-\frac13a^3\Gamma(11/4).
\]
Now
\[
\Gamma(7/4)=\frac34\Gamma(3/4),
\qquad
\Gamma(11/4)=\frac{21}{16}\Gamma(3/4),
\]
so
\[
B=\left(\frac{3a}{16}-\frac{7a^3}{16}\right)\Gamma(3/4).
\]
Since \(a^2=(2/3)^3=8/27\),
\[
B=\frac{a}{16}\left(3-\frac{56}{27}\right)\Gamma(3/4)
=\frac{25a}{432}\Gamma(3/4).
\]
Finally \(a=(2/3)^{3/2}=2\sqrt6/9\), hence
\[
B=\frac{25\sqrt6}{1944}\Gamma(3/4).
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{25\sqrt6}{1944}\Gamma(3/4)}
\]
